import datetime
try:
    HOL = set(['2026-10-26', '2026-11-11', '2026-11-26', '2026-12-25', '2027-01-01'])
    WD = ['Monday','Tuesday','Wednesday','Thursday','Friday','Saturday','Sunday']
    MO = ['January','February','March','April','May','June','July','August','September','October','November','December']
    raw = str(vars.get('now') or '').strip()
    try:
        nowdt = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(raw[:16])
    except Exception:
        nowdt = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(raw[:10] + 'T09:00')
    today = nowdt.date()
    def isbd(d):
        return d.weekday() < 5 and d.isoformat() not in HOL
    def txt(d):
        return WD[d.weekday()] + ' ' + str(d.day) + ' ' + MO[d.month-1] + ' ' + str(d.year)
    def addbd(d, n):
        c = 0
        while c < n:
            d = d + datetime.timedelta(days=1)
            if isbd(d):
                c += 1
        return d
    nbd = addbd(today, 1)
    vars['today_iso'] = today.isoformat()
    vars['today_text'] = txt(today)
    vars['now_time'] = nowdt.strftime('%H:%M')
    lines = []
    cur = nowdt.strftime('%H:%M')
    if cur < '19:00':
        start = '10:00' if cur < '10:00' else 'after ' + cur
        lines.append('Today, ' + txt(today) + ' (' + today.isoformat() + '), from ' + start + ' up to 19:00.')
    lines.append(txt(nbd) + ' (' + nbd.isoformat() + '), from 10:00 up to 19:00 included.')
    tom = today + datetime.timedelta(days=1)
    extra = 'Tomorrow is ' + txt(tom) + '.'
    if tom != nbd:
        extra += ' Tomorrow is NOT allowed, it is not a business day.'
    vars['callback_text'] = 'The ONLY allowed callback times are:\n- ' + '\n- '.join(lines) + '\n' + extra + ' Any other day or time is outside the window.'
    # week tables
    monday = today - datetime.timedelta(days=today.weekday())
    tab = []
    for i in range(7):
        a = monday + datetime.timedelta(days=i)
        b = a + datetime.timedelta(days=7)
        t1 = '"this ' + WD[i] + '" = ' + txt(a) + (' (already past)' if a < today else '')
        tab.append(t1 + '; "next ' + WD[i] + '" = ' + txt(b))
    vars['weekday_table'] = '\n'.join(tab)
    # last business day of this week, else of next week
    def lastbd(mon):
        for k in range(4, -1, -1):
            d = mon + datetime.timedelta(days=k)
            if isbd(d):
                return d
        return None
    a1 = lastbd(monday)
    if a1 is None or a1 <= today:
        a1 = lastbd(monday + datetime.timedelta(days=7))
    vars['attempt1_date'] = a1.isoformat()
    vars['early_deadline'] = addbd(today, 12).isoformat()
    vars['late_deadline'] = addbd(today, 7).isoformat()
    vars['setup_state'] = 'ok'
except Exception as e:
    vars['setup_state'] = 'error ' + str(e)
    vars.setdefault('callback_text', 'Callbacks: today later than now up to 19:00, or the next business day from 10:00 to 19:00.')
    vars.setdefault('today_text', str(vars.get('now')))
    vars.setdefault('weekday_table', '')

import datetime, json, re
try:
    HOL = set(['2026-10-26', '2026-11-11', '2026-11-26', '2026-12-25', '2027-01-01'])
    WD = ['Monday','Tuesday','Wednesday','Thursday','Friday','Saturday','Sunday']
    MO = ['January','February','March','April','May','June','July','August','September','October','November','December']
    def isbd(d):
        return d.weekday() < 5 and d.isoformat() not in HOL
    def txt(d):
        return WD[d.weekday()] + ' ' + str(d.day) + ' ' + MO[d.month-1]
    def fmt(x):
        try:
            x = float(x)
        except Exception:
            return str(x)
        s = '%.2f' % x
        return s[:-3] if s.endswith('.00') else s
    prods = vars.get('products')
    if isinstance(prods, str):
        try:
            prods = json.loads(prods)
        except Exception:
            prods = None
    if not isinstance(prods, list) or not prods:
        found = dict()
        for k, v in list(vars.items()):
            m = re.search(r'products\.(\d+)\.(\w+)$', str(k))
            if m:
                found.setdefault(int(m.group(1)), dict())[m.group(2)] = v
        prods = [found[i] for i in sorted(found)]
    prods = [p for p in prods if isinstance(p, dict)]
    today = datetime.date.fromisoformat(str(vars.get('today_iso')))
    a1base = datetime.date.fromisoformat(str(vars.get('attempt1_date')))
    early = datetime.date.fromisoformat(str(vars.get('early_deadline')))
    late = datetime.date.fromisoformat(str(vars.get('late_deadline')))
    infos = []
    for i, p in enumerate(prods):
        ptype = str(p.get('type') or '')
        pid = str(p.get('product_id') or ('p' + str(i + 1)))
        if ptype == 'credit_card':
            words = 'credit card ending ' + str(p.get('card_last4') or '')
            floor = p.get('minimum_payment'); floor_name = 'minimum payment'
        else:
            words = ptype.replace('_', ' ') if ptype else 'loan'
            floor = p.get('instalment_amount'); floor_name = 'instalment'
        past_due = float(p.get('past_due') or 0)
        try:
            floor = float(floor)
        except Exception:
            floor = past_due
        dl = int(float(p.get('days_late') or 0))
        if dl <= 7:
            band = 'early'; att = 1; deadline = early
        else:
            band = 'late'; att = 2; deadline = late
        a1 = a1base if a1base <= deadline else deadline
        infos.append(dict(pid=pid, words=words, past_due=past_due, floor=floor, floor_name=floor_name, dl=dl, band=band, att=att, deadline=deadline, a1=a1))
        vars['dl_' + pid] = deadline.isoformat()
        vars['pd_' + pid] = str(past_due)
    n = len(infos)
    vars['n_products'] = str(n)
    vars['pids_csv'] = ','.join(x['pid'] for x in infos)
    vars['open_pids'] = vars['pids_csv']
    vars['rec_pids'] = ''
    vars['note_log'] = ''
    vars['all_done'] = 'no'
    lines = []
    for x in infos:
        l = x['pid'] + ' = ' + x['words'] + ': full past-due amount ' + fmt(x['past_due']) + ', ' + str(x['dl']) + ' days late (' + x['band'] + ' band). '
        l += 'Floor (lowest amount allowed) ' + fmt(x['floor']) + ' (the ' + x['floor_name'] + '). '
        l += 'Deadline (latest date allowed) ' + txt(x['deadline']) + ' (' + x['deadline'].isoformat() + '). '
        l += 'Attempt 1: propose ' + fmt(x['past_due']) + ' (or the floor ' + fmt(x['floor']) + ' if the customer already said the full amount is too much) on ' + txt(x['a1']) + ' (' + x['a1'].isoformat() + '). '
        if x['att'] >= 2:
            l += 'Attempt 2: propose the floor ' + fmt(x['floor']) + ' on the deadline ' + txt(x['deadline']) + '. Persuasion attempts allowed: 2.'
        else:
            l += 'NO attempt 2: persuasion attempts allowed: 1.'
        lines.append('- ' + l)
    vars['products_text'] = '\n'.join(lines)
    if n == 1:
        x = infos[0]
        st = 'Thank you, ' + str(vars.get('title') or '') + ' ' + str(vars.get('last_name') or '') + '. I am calling from the collections team about a late payment on your ' + x['words'] + '. The past-due amount is ' + fmt(x['past_due']) + ', and it is ' + str(x['dl']) + ' days late. Can you make this payment today?'
    else:
        st = 'Thank you, ' + str(vars.get('title') or '') + ' ' + str(vars.get('last_name') or '') + '. I am calling from the collections team about late payments on ' + str(n) + ' of your products. '
        for x in infos:
            st += 'Your ' + x['words'] + ' has ' + fmt(x['past_due']) + ' past due, ' + str(x['dl']) + ' days late. '
        st += 'Can you pay all of them today?'
    vars['statement_text'] = st
    maxdl = max([x['deadline'] for x in infos] or [today])
    cal = []
    d = today
    while d <= maxdl + datetime.timedelta(days=10):
        nb = d
        while not isbd(nb):
            nb = nb + datetime.timedelta(days=1)
        if isbd(d):
            ok = [x['pid'] for x in infos if d <= x['deadline']]
            bad = [x['pid'] for x in infos if d > x['deadline']]
            tag = 'business day.'
            if ok:
                tag += ' Allowed for ' + ', '.join(ok) + '.'
            if bad:
                tag += ' AFTER THE DEADLINE of ' + ', '.join(bad) + ' (use that product\'s deadline instead).'
        else:
            tag = ('weekend' if d.weekday() >= 5 else 'bank holiday') + ', NOT allowed -> offer the next business day ' + txt(nb) + ' (' + nb.isoformat() + ') where it is not after the deadline.'
        cal.append(d.isoformat() + ' ' + txt(d) + ('  (today)' if d == today else '') + ': ' + tag)
        d = d + datetime.timedelta(days=1)
    vars['calendar_text'] = '\n'.join(cal)
    vars['prepare_state'] = 'ok'
except Exception as e:
    vars['prepare_state'] = 'error ' + str(e)
    vars.setdefault('products_text', 'Product data could not be prepared.')
    vars.setdefault('statement_text', 'Thank you. I am calling from the collections team about a late payment. Can you make this payment today?')
    vars.setdefault('calendar_text', '')
    vars.setdefault('pids_csv', 'p1')
    vars.setdefault('open_pids', 'p1')
    vars.setdefault('all_done', 'no')

negotiate.task_message:
The customer is verified. You have just stated every late product and asked whether they can pay (all of them) today. Now get payment promises.

ORDER OF WORK
A. If they can pay everything today: the promises are the full amount of each product, today. Go to READ-BACK.
B. If they name ONE date (and no amount) for everything: each product gets its full amount on that date, checked per product against the CALENDAR. If that date is after a product's deadline, that product gets ITS OWN deadline instead and you say so in the read-back; the other products keep the named date. Go to READ-BACK.
C. Otherwise go through the products ONE BY ONE in the order of PRODUCTS. Do not ask about today again. For each product start at its attempt 1: propose its full amount on its attempt 1 date, unless the customer already named a date or amount for it. Settle one product (agreed, or finally refused) before moving to the next.

RULES PER PRODUCT
1. You propose every amount. NEVER ask how much they can pay.
2. A date or an amount the customer proposes is never a refusal. Check it:
   - Date: look it up in the CALENDAR. Allowed for that product -> accept. Weekend or bank holiday not after the deadline -> offer the next business day shown. After that product's deadline -> say the latest date you can record for it is its deadline and offer it; if they refuse that, it is a flat refusal.
   - Vague period ('next week', 'end of the month', 'when my salary comes') -> ask once for the exact day. If they still give none, propose that product's deadline.
   - 'next <weekday>' / 'this <weekday>': use WEEKDAY WORDS.
   - Amount from the floor up to the full amount, both included -> accept. Below the floor -> say it cannot be recorded and offer the floor once; if not accepted, it is a flat refusal.
3. Full amount too much -> offer that product's floor once and say the rest stays overdue. Floor refused -> flat refusal.
4. A flat refusal (a no with no date and no amount, a non-answer, refusing your offer) uses one persuasion attempt of THAT product. Attempts are counted per product: attempt 1 and attempt 2 exactly as in PRODUCTS. When that product's attempts are used up and they refuse again, that product is refused: stop, never repeat an offer, and move to the next product.
5. 'I already paid' this product -> say payments can take one business day to appear; no promise for it (reason paid). 'Not mine' / 'never had it' / 'it was closed or paid off' -> do not argue; no promise for it (reason dispute). Then continue with the other products.

READ-BACK AND RECORDING (only when every product is settled)
6. If at least one product is agreed: read back ALL agreed promises together in one turn (product in words, amount, date as weekday day month, and say when a product uses its own deadline) and ask "Do you confirm?". If they change something, check it and read back again. After a clear yes, call create_promise once per agreed product, one per message, product_id from PRODUCTS, amount as a number, date as YYYY-MM-DD.
7. If create_promise fails, call it once more. Never say a promise is recorded unless the result says so. If it fails twice, tell the customer you could not record that one, then call add_note with reason service_error for it.
8. Then, for EVERY product without a recorded promise, call add_note with its product_id and reason: refused, hardship, dispute, paid or service_error. This applies even when no product got a promise. The call is closed for you automatically once every product has a promise or a note.

OTHER
- Never offer a discount, waiver, payment plan or any other term.
- If they ask for a human: the first time, ask whether you can help them yourself. If they insist, call transfer_to_agent (and never add_note).
- If they say twice that they do not want to talk: every product without a promise is refused; call add_note for each.
- If they ask to change or cancel a recorded promise: they can do it in the mobile app.
- If they ask something these facts do not answer, say you do not have that information.
- Follow what_to_do_next in every tool result. After every tool result, speak to the customer or call the next tool.

PRODUCTS (in get_account order)
{{products_text}}
DATES
- Today: {{today_text}} ({{today_iso}}).
- A promise date must be a business day (Monday to Friday, not a bank holiday) from today up to THAT product's deadline.
WEEKDAY WORDS
{{weekday_table}}
CALENDAR (look every date up here)
{{calendar_text}}

except Exception:
    vars['decline_route'] = 'retry'

function.name: end_call
function.description:
This is used to technically terminate the call after all the customer's questions have been answered and necessary information has been provided.
- It should only be triggered SILENTLY in the background after the customer-related workflow is complete; never mention this tool or its name to the customer.

llmConfig.systemPrompt: You are a helpful assistant. Your role is to help users with their tasks. Always be friendly and professional. You can use `end_call` tool after you say goodbye to customer to hang up if call about to finish.

workflow.system_prompt:
You are Freya Bank's digital assistant on an outbound phone call to {{title}} {{last_name}}. Speak English. Keep every turn to one or two short sentences. Address the customer as {{title}} {{last_name}}.
Always:
- If asked whether you are a robot or an AI: say you are Freya Bank's digital assistant, then continue.
- If asked whether this is a scam: say they can verify this call by phoning Freya Bank's customer service number, then continue.
- Never invent figures, dates or reasons. If you do not have the information, say so.
- Never offer a discount, waiver, payment plan or any term you were not given.
- Do not say goodbye or end the call yourself: the call is closed for you.
- Call at most one tool per message. When a rule says to call a tool, call it: saying it is not enough.
- After every tool result, speak to the customer or call the next tool. Never end a turn with nothing. Follow what_to_do_next in a tool result.
- Say amounts as plain numbers, for example 420.50, and dates as weekday, day and month, for example Friday 16 October.
